questions.text:
Consider the Karnaugh map given below, where x represents "don't care" and blank represents 0.

Assume for all inputs (a, b, c, d) the respective complements [latex](\bar{a},\bar{b},\bar{c},\bar{d})[/latex] are also available. The above logic is implemented 2-input NOR gates only. The minimum number of gates required is ____________.
questions.solution:
The 1s (with suitable don't-cares) form one group: all cells with c = 1 and a = 0. So [latex]f=c\bar a[/latex].

[latex]c\bar a=\overline{\bar c+a}=NOR(\bar c,a)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] a single 2-input NOR gate (complements are available).

Answer: 1

questions.text:
When two 8-bit numbers [latex]A_{7}....A_{0}[/latex] and [latex]B_{7}....B_{0}[/latex] in 2's complement representation (with [latex]A_{0}[/latex]
and [latex]B_{0}[/latex] as the least significant bits ) are added using a ripple-carry Combinational Circuit, the sum bits
obtained are  [latex]S_{7}....S_{0}[/latex] and the carry bits are  [latex]C_{7}....C_{0}[/latex]. An overflow is said to have occurred if
questions.solution:
2's complement overflow happens when both operands have the same sign but the sum has the other sign:
- both negative ([latex]A_7=B_7=1[/latex]) and [latex]S_7=0[/latex], or
- both positive ([latex]A_7=B_7=0[/latex]) and [latex]S_7=1[/latex].

That is [latex]A_7B_7\bar S_7+\bar A_7\bar B_7S_7=1[/latex].

Answer: Option 3

questions.text:
The n-bit fixed-point representation of an unsigned real number real X uses f bits for the
fraction part. Let i=n-f. The range of decimal values for X in this representation is
questions.solution:
i integer bits and f fraction bits. The smallest value is 0 (all bits 0). The largest has all bits 1: [latex](2^i-1)+(1-2^{-f})=2^i-2^{-f}[/latex].

Answer: 0 to [latex]2^i-2^{-f}[/latex]

questions.text: The functional difference between SR flip-flop and J-K flip-flop is that :
questions.solution:
In an SR flip-flop, S = R = 1 is not allowed. A JK flip-flop accepts J = K = 1 and simply toggles.

Answer: J-K flip-flop accepts both inputs 1

questions.text: Which of the following binary number is the same as its 2's complement ?
questions.solution:
2's complement of 1000: invert [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0111, add 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1000. It equals itself (it is [latex]-[/latex]8, the most negative 4-bit number). The other options change.

Answer: 1000
